title: Link upstream Hello
description: Spec 63. The Hello a dialer sends to be granted the upstream role. It carries one typed api_key credential (never a registration credential), no registration connection id, exactly the two features iw.link-upstream/1 and iw.link-http-json/1, a fresh link_incarnation_id per dial, and a channel_binding: the lowercase hex SHA-256 over the transport exporter, the incarnation id and the dialer id. The binding is replay resistance across channels, not proof of possession of the key; TLS protects the key. Closed: an acceptor that reads this Hello refuses unknown members of the shape below, although the wire decoder of the reference implementation ignores unknown members of a Hello (a refused Hello gets no acknowledgement, so the refusal is silent). link-hello.json describes the same frame for a legacy peer and stays open.

node_id.description: The dialing gateway's id: no whitespace, control character, comma or equals sign (the list-token alphabet of the federation path). U+FEFF is excluded by name: ECMA-262 `\s` contains it, Python's `re` and Rust's `char::is_whitespace` do not.

credential.description: The api_key secret. Never logged, never in argv or a URL; a fixture carries an obviously fake value.
